files.lesson.md: --- order: 10 unit: solids node: AC9M7SP01 n1 title: Nets summary: "A net is a flat pattern that folds into a solid. Six squares make a cube only if they land on six different faces; a triangular prism has two triangles and three rectangles." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A cereal box starts as one flat piece of card. Which flat shapes fold up into a box, and which ones jam?" connection: box-net app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8295 url: http://127.0.0.1:8295/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: nets.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A cross of six squares folds into a cube: each square lands on a different face." } explainClip: query: { code: "@nets.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "From a row to a net" say: "Six squares in a row do not fold. Move two and it works." clip: - caption: { text: "Six squares in a row: some land on the same face.", say: "Six squares in a row. Some land on the same face." } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Take the last two squares away.", say: "Take the last two squares away." } - click: Square at column 6, row 2, in the net (press to remove) - click: Square at column 5, row 2, in the net (press to remove) - caption: { text: "Add one square above and one below.", say: "Add one above, and one below." } - click: Square at column 2, row 1, empty (press to add) - click: Square at column 2, row 3, empty (press to add) - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "folds into a cube" } - wait: 1500 --- A **net** is a flat pattern that folds up into a solid. A cube's net is six squares joined along their edges. A **prism** is a solid with two matching ends and flat rectangular sides; the net of a triangular prism is two triangles and three rectangles. ## Predict: six in a row ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to whether six squares in a row fold into a cube shows whether they count squares or picture the fold." check: type: predict q: "Six squares joined in a straight row. Will they fold into a cube?" options: ["No: some squares would land on top of each other", "Yes: a cube has six faces", "Only if the row is bent"] actual: "No. Fold the row round and the sixth square lands on the first. A net needs six squares on six different faces." ``` Picture wrapping the row round a cube: where does the fifth square go? ## Run: fold the net ```step stage: run insight: "Changing the squares of a net and watching the board fold it shows that a net works only when all six squares land on different faces." try: { playground: board, starter: "nets.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Click squares to change the row until the board says it folds into a cube. Was your prediction right?", when: "f = 1", explain: "Folding needs six squares on six different faces. A row of six wraps back on itself." } ``` Click a square to add it or take it away. The colours show which face each square becomes. ## Investigate: six squares is not enough ```step stage: investigate insight: "Six squares is necessary but not enough (Zara counts only); the test is whether the faces differ; a prism net adds up its faces." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A net folds into a cube. How many squares does it have?" answer: "6" explain: "A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#zara" text: "Zara says her block of six squares folds into a cube. Click the line where her reasoning goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: net-count-only explain: "Line 4: six squares is needed, but they must land on six different faces. A 2 by 3 block has squares that fold on top of each other." - check: type: question q: "What is the best way to test a net for a cube?" options: ["Fold it (or roll a cube over it) and check that every face is covered once", "Count that it has six squares", "Check that it is a rectangle", "Check that it is symmetrical"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Six squares is needed, but a row of six fails.", "A 2 by 3 block is a rectangle and does not fold.", "A row of six is symmetrical and does not fold."] explain: "Fold it, in your head or on the board: each face must be covered exactly once." ``` ### How many squares? Think about the faces of the cube. ### Find the mistake Read Zara's reasoning. What else must be true? ### The test ## Modify: other nets and other solids ```step stage: modify insight: "Different cube nets (a cross, six squares that fail) and the prism's net area: faces of a prism are two ends and a rectangle for each side." try: { playground: board, starter: "nets.yml#modify", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "nets.yml#modify" hint: ["Start with a row of 4 squares.", "Add one square above and one below the row."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a net of a cube with a row of four squares in the middle.", when: "f = 1 and c = 6", explain: "Four in a row with one above and one below folds: the row wraps round and the extra squares are the top and bottom." } - starter: "nets.yml#cross" hint: ["Move one square so that two squares would land on the same face.", "A row of five with one square on top does not fold."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a net with six squares that does not fold into a cube.", when: "c = 6 and f = 0", explain: "For example a row of five with one square on top, a 2 by 3 block, or the row of six: two squares land on the same face." } - starter: "nets.yml#prism" hint: ["The net area is the area of 2 triangles plus 3 rectangles.", "Slide the length L to 5."] check: { type: board, text: "The triangle has sides 3, 4 and 5 cm. Set the length to 5 cm. What is the net's area?", when: "L = 5", explain: "Two triangles of 6 cm² and rectangles 3 × 5, 4 × 5 and 5 × 5: 12 + 60 = 72 cm²." } - check: type: question q: "How many rectangles are in the net of a triangular prism?" options: ["3", "2", "4", "5"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Those are the two triangles.", "A triangle has three sides, not four.", "That is the total number of faces."] explain: "One rectangle for each side of the triangle: 3, plus the 2 triangles makes 5 faces." ``` ### A cross ### Six squares that fail ### A prism ### Count the rectangles ## Practise: nets ```step stage: practise insight: "Prism surface area and other nets, mixed; counting faces is the planted slip; the triangle area review keeps the prism's end faces fresh." try: { playground: board, starter: "nets.yml#prism-free", height: 600 } tasks: - check: type: question q: "What is the net of a square pyramid made of?" options: ["1 square and 4 triangles", "4 squares and 1 triangle", "2 squares and 4 triangles", "5 squares"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The base is a square and the sides are triangles.", "A pyramid has one base.", "That is the net of an open box."] explain: "A square base and four triangles that meet at the point." - starter: "nets.yml#prism-free" check: { type: board, text: "A prism has a right triangle with sides 6, 8 and 10 cm and length 5 cm. Set the board to match.", when: "a = 6 and b = 8 and L = 5", explain: "Two triangles of 24 cm² and rectangles 6 × 5, 8 × 5 and 10 × 5: 48 + 120 = 168 cm²." } - check: type: answer q: "Read the net's area on the board. The prism's surface area is how many square centimetres?" answer: "168" feedback: - ["84", "The net is the whole surface laid flat, so there is no halving."] explain: "The net is the surface laid flat, so its area is the surface area." - check: type: answer q: "Review: a triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. What is its area in square centimetres?" answer: "20" feedback: - ["40", "That is base × height. A triangle is half of that."] explain: "(8 × 5) ÷ 2 = 20 cm²." - check: type: question q: "How many rectangles are in the net of a rectangular prism (a box)?" options: ["6", "4", "5", "3"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Those are the sides only; the top and bottom are rectangles too.", "A box has 6 faces.", "Opposite faces are the same size, but all six are drawn."] explain: "A box has 6 faces, all rectangles, in 3 matching pairs (some may be squares)." ``` ### A pyramid ### Surface area ### Net area ### Review: triangle area ### A box ## Make: a net to fit ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing the length of a prism to meet a target area applies the net as faces added up." try: { playground: board, starter: "nets.yml#prism-free", height: 600 } hint: ["Each extra centimetre of length adds 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm² with a 3, 4, 5 triangle.", "The two triangles give 12 cm² whatever the length."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a prism net with a surface area between 90 and 100 cm². Use a 3, 4, 5 triangle.", when: "a = 3 and b = 4 and A > 90 and A < 100", explain: "With a 3, 4, 5 triangle the area is 12 + 12 × L, so L = 7 gives 96 cm²." } ``` Then: why does a net show the surface area exactly, when a 3D drawing does not? ## Make: a gift box, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A gift box net is its six faces laid flat, so the card needed is the sum of six areas; pairs of equal faces shorten the sum." hint: ["List the faces: how many, and which are the same?", "Find each face's area, then add them."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A gift box for a mug is 10 cm long, 10 cm wide and 12 cm tall. How much card does its net need for the six faces, in cm², with no flaps?" steps: - ["The top and bottom are each 10 × 10 = 100 cm², so together 200 cm²", "two matching square faces"] - ["The four sides are each 10 × 12 = 120 cm², so together 480 cm²", "four matching rectangles"] - ["200 + 480 = 680 cm²", "the net is all six faces laid flat, so add their areas"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why add the areas of all six faces?" options: - "The net is the six faces laid flat, so its area is all of them added" - "Only the four sides need card" - "You multiply the three lengths" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The top and bottom need card too.", "That gives the volume, the space inside, not the card."] answer: "680" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["1200", "That is 10 × 10 × 12, the volume. The card covers the faces: add their areas."] - ["480", "That is only the four sides. The top and bottom need card too."] criteria: - "I listed all six faces and which ones match." - "I found each area before adding." - "I did not count the volume." explain: "2 × 100 + 4 × 120 = 200 + 480 = 680 cm². The net lays all six faces flat." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The box size is made up for the task, and a real box also needs flaps for glue. Draw the net, label the faces, then type the area. **Also used in** - **Packaging.** Boxes, cartons and bags start as flat printed card, cut and folded from one net. - **Wrapping.** Gift wrap for a box needs about the area of its net, plus an overlap. ```teacher summary: Students build nets on a grid and watch the board fold them into a cube, then find the net area of a triangular prism (AC9M7SP01, node 1). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can tell whether a net folds into a cube, and say how I know. - I can name the faces in the net of a prism or a pyramid. - I can find the surface area of a triangular prism from its net. struggle: Picturing the fold. Let students build a cube from paper or linking squares beside the board; the board's colours say where each square lands. before: > Do the Run board yourself first, then fold a real cube net from card if you have time. The one idea: a net works only if every face is covered exactly once. Counting six squares is necessary but not enough (Zara's mistake). The board folds by rolling a cube over the squares, so the colour on each square is the face it becomes. The cube has 11 different nets; the Make task is not about finding all of them (see Stretch). running: - "Predict: ask which square would land on the first one." - "Run: ask students to find a net before they check it on the board." - "Investigate: ask what Zara could do to check her block." - "Modify: for the prism, ask which side of the triangle each rectangle matches." - "Make: ask why the area has two parts, the ends and the sides." - "Make on paper: ask how many faces are the same, and why the volume is not the answer." stuck: - see: A student says any six joined squares fold into a cube. ask: Which two squares would land on the same face? fix: Roll the cube across the squares, or fold a paper copy. - see: A student forgets the two triangles when finding a prism's area. ask: How many faces does a triangular prism have? fix: "Five faces: three rectangles and two triangles." - see: A student halves the net area. ask: Is the net the whole surface or only part? fix: The net is the whole surface laid flat. stretch: A cube has 11 different nets (turning or flipping a net does not count as new). Can you find them all? support: Give students six linking squares or a card net to fold before the board. leads: > This starts AC9M7SP01. Where it leads: views and isometric drawings (next lesson); surface area and volume of prisms (Measurement); Year 8 volume of prisms and cylinders. exit: q: A net of six squares has four in a row, one above and one below. Does it fold into a cube? How can you tell? a: Yes. The row of four wraps round the sides, and the extra two squares are the top and the bottom, so every face is covered once. explain: > A **net** is a solid unfolded flat. A cube's net is six squares that fold to cover all six faces once; six squares alone is not enough, so test by folding. A triangular prism's net is two triangles (the ends) and three rectangles (one for each side of the triangle). Its area is the surface area. ```

# Nets to build and fold for "Nets". The cube board starts with the squares in a row.

# region: run
widget: net
mode: cube
cells: 0,1; 1,1; 2,1; 3,1; 4,1; 5,1
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: net
mode: cube
cells: 0,1; 1,1; 2,1; 3,1; 4,1; 5,1
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: net
mode: cube
cells: 1,0; 0,1; 1,1; 2,1; 3,1; 1,2
# endregion

# region: modify
widget: net
mode: cube
cells: 0,1; 1,1; 2,1; 3,1; 4,1; 5,1
# endregion

# region: cross
widget: net
mode: cube
cells: 1,0; 0,1; 1,1; 2,1; 3,1; 1,2
# endregion

# region: prism
widget: net
mode: prism
a: 3
b: 4
slider L: 1, 8, 3
units: cm
# endregion

# region: prism-free
widget: net
mode: prism
slider a: 1, 10, 3
slider b: 1, 10, 4
slider L: 1, 8, 3
units: cm
# endregion
